title: Feature Expansion for Graph Neural Networks
summary: The paper analyzes the feature space of spatial and spectral GNNs and argues that repeated aggregation creates linearly correlated subspaces bounded by weight sharing and low-dimensional node attributes. It proposes FE-GNN, which flattens feature subspaces by assigning independent weights to each subspace and augments the feature space with truncated-SVD structural principal components. On random 60/20/20 splits, FE-GNN (C) reaches 73.33% accuracy on Chameleon and reports large heterophilic gains over baselines.

match_target.why: The user explicitly targets Table 2, FE-GNN (C) node classification accuracy on Chameleon; it is a central heterophilic result and requires only one dataset/model, not the full multi-dataset average or side ablation.

tolerance.why: Rule 3: the target is bounded accuracy on Chameleon, whose 20% test set has about 455 nodes (<2,000); the paper prints ±0.35 as a 95% confidence interval, not repeated-run std, so use 2.0 absolute points.

requirements.stmt: The FE-GNN implementation must be purely linear, without activation functions or dropout, using only cross-entropy loss.
requirements.quote: our implementation is purely linear without any deep artifices such as activation functions or dropout except for the cross-entropy loss

requirements.stmt: The model must compute H = sum_{k=0}^K Pk(Lhat) X W(k) + S Ws with independent weights for each feature subspace.
requirements.quote: H = K X k=0 Pk(ˆL)XW (k) + SWs

requirements.stmt: FE-GNN (C) must use Chebyshev polynomials for Pk(Lhat).
requirements.quote: FE-GNN uses the Chebyshev or monomial polynomials to construct the feature space

requirements.stmt: Chebyshev polynomials must be generated by P0(x)=1, P1(x)=x, Pk(x)=2xPk-1 - Pk-2.
requirements.quote: Tk(x) denotes Chebyshev polynomial P0(x) = 1, P1(x) = x, Pk(x) = 2xPk−1 −Pk−2.

requirements.stmt: The graph structure matrix must use the re-normalized adjacency with self-loops and symmetric degree normalization.
The structural expansion subspace S must be constructed from a truncated SVD of the structural matrix.
S should contain principal components and corresponding singular values from the truncated SVD.
requirements.quote: where  ̃Q,  ̃V are the principal components and the corresponding singular values

requirements.stmt: Each column of the constructed feature space must be normalized so columns contribute equally.
requirements.quote: we add a column-wise normalization to ensure that each column of each feature subspace contributes equally to the whole feature space

requirements.stmt: Column-wise normalization should be applied to the concatenated feature space F, not only to individual subspaces.
requirements.quote: Column-wise normalization is defined as forcing ∥F·i∥2 = 1, where we take F as the concatenation of the feature space

requirements.stmt: Node classification must use random 60% train, 20% validation, 20% test splits.
requirements.quote: 60% as the training set, 20% as the validation set, and 20% as the test set

requirements.stmt: Reported results should summarize 100 runs over random splits/seeds.
requirements.quote: We test on the node classification task with random 60%/20%/20% splits and summarize the results of 100 runs

requirements.stmt: Optimization must use Adam with the paper's early-stopping/max-epoch description.
requirements.quote: We employ Adam for optimization and set the early stopping criteria as a warmup of 50 pluses patience of 200

requirements.stmt: Training should cap at 100 epochs as stated in the appendix.
requirements.quote: patience of 200 for a maximum of 100 epochs

requirements.stmt: The reported metric is average accuracy, also described as micro F1, with a 95% confidence interval.
requirements.quote: We report the average accuracy (micro F1 score) in the classification task with a 95% confidence interval in all the tables and figures

requirements.stmt: For Chameleon FE-GNN, use lr=0.01, weight decay=0.0005, |S|=700, hidden size=64, k=3.
Datasets must be treated as undirected graphs.
requirements.quote: We set these datasets to undirected graphs as we assumed in the Preliminaries
